text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Alfred Sant speaks of social need for divorce and says commission will be set up this year to study issue. Opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami, who opposes divorce, said he hoped Malta would never feel the need for it because it would weaken the institution of marriage. The leaders were speaking at a university debate on whether divorce should be introduced in Malta, a staunchly Catholic country which does not have have divorce.
- Chamber of Commerce says Gozo ferry fares rise will harm tourism to the island. Fare rises were announced on January 26.
- Prime Minister Sant says divorce should come to Malta.
- Gozo ferry fares reduce island residents to second class citizens.

- Inquiry in Malta family's gassing in Rome hotel to end shortly. The family was staying in a hotel for one night in December when gas leaked into the room. A young woman was killed and her parents remain in coma.
